  "text": "Martin arrived at the allotment with a kettle under his arm. His sister was kneeling beside a row of onions, pressing the soil around each stem.

“The switch sticks,” he said.

“Then why bring it?”

“It still boils.”

Ruth sat back on her heels. The kettle was the yellow one from their mother’s kitchen. There was a brown mark below the spout that no amount of scrubbing had shifted.

“I’ve got a flask.”

“For when people visit.”

“You’re the only person who visits.”

He carried it into the shed. She heard him moving flowerpots along the bench.

“There’s no electricity, Martin.”

He came to the doorway, still holding it.

“No. Of course.”

Ruth pulled another onion from the tray. Its roots had tangled with the next one, and she worked them apart without looking up.

“Have you finished the kitchen?” she asked.

“Nearly.”

“What’s left?”

“The drawer by the cooker.”

Their mother had kept string in it, and batteries, and instructions for things she no longer owned.

“Leave that,” Ruth said. “I’ll come Sunday.”

He put the kettle on the bench outside. Then he folded his coat over the chair and crouched at the end of the row.

“How deep?”

“Just cover the white bit.”

She passed him the tray.

They planted six before he spoke again.

“There are three tea bags inside it.”

Ruth brushed soil from her wrist.

“In the kettle?”

“I thought you might need some.”

She stood and fetched the flask from the shed. Martin rinsed two plant labels in the water butt while she looked for the cups."
